deviations: Bandwidth sample taken as |dif| <= 45 (dif = months older than December 1955; dif=0 is December 1955, treated). The paper's equation writes an open interval (c-h, c+h); the closed version was chosen because the text says 'born within 45 months'.

Anderson (2008) indices: items standardized by control-group (born Jan 1956 or later, before1955==0) mean and SD over all respondents answering every SRQ-20 item (full sample, not just the bandwidth); weights are row sums of the inverse covariance matrix of the standardized items; the weighted index is re-standardized to mean 0, SD 1 in the control group.

Observation counts are complete cases (outcome, treatment, running variable, education, ethnicity, female, birth month, province, surveyor) in the bandwidth, i.e. without dropping fixed-effect singletons (fixest drops 15-16 singletons in estimation, which does not change the point estimates).
notes: Exploratory attempt-1 listed variables (no RESULT lines). Final script: sample excludes survey non-respondents (non_response==1); OLS of outcome on before1955, dif and dif*before1955 (linear separately on each side, uniform kernel), with education and ethnicity category dummies, female, and birth-month, province and surveyor fixed effects, SEs clustered by month-year of birth (dif), via fixest::feols. SRQ sum and indices defined only for respondents answering all 20 items. Used the dataset's head_ache variable as 'frequent headaches'. The ICPSR 'read me .pdf' was not opened. No run hung.
